subject: Re: RAG pilot - next steps & eval plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Irwin <sam@acme.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: RAG pilot kickoff - recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Priya -

Thanks again for a productive kickoff this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into the pilot: 

Recap:
- Primary objective: reduce erroneous answers in support KB lookups and improve answer grounding for short-form responses (<= 200 tokens).
- High-value docs: product FAQs, release notes, policy docs (we'll index ~45k docs to start).
- Success metrics: grounding precision@3 >= 0.88, end-to-end latency p95 <= 700ms (regional), hallucination rate reduction > 50% vs baseline.

Redwood initial recommendations (for eval phase):
1) Models to evaluate (recommended order):
   - Mistral-Instruct-22B (instruction-tuned dense model) - baseline for throughput/quality balance
   - Llama-3-70B-Quant (llama-3 family, 4-bit quant) - best quality ceiling for grounding tests
   - Redwood-OpenRerank-Base (smaller instruct model for reranking & hallucination debugging)

2) Retrieval + reranker settings:
   - Retriever: hybrid dense (FAISS IVFFlat, embedding model: ada-embedding-2) + BM25 fallback
   - Initial top_k retrieve = 12, rerank top_k = 6 (use reranker for precision@k tuning)
   - Reranker: cross-encoder MonoBERT-v1 (we recommend starting with headroom at bias=0.15 to favor precision)

3) Prompt and grounding strategy:
   - Use source citations in response with snippet-level highlights (show 1-2 snippets per result)
   - Safety filter: drop sources older than retention policy (start with 3-year window) unless explicitly requested

4) Eval plan + artifacts we will deliver:
   - Shared prompt set (50 canonical queries + 150 random production-ish queries) - attached as acme_prompt_sets_v1.zip
   - Benchmark results template & current baseline CSV - attached
   - Dashboard links with precision@k, ROUGE-like overlap, and hallucination rate per prompt set

Action items / next steps:
- Redwood: deliver SOW draft + pilot run plan by next Tue (6/14) - attached: acme_rag_eval_plan.pdf
- ACME: provide sample export of target KB (S3 link preferred) and a list of 20 representative queries by EOD Fri 6/11
- Schedule 30m model selection sync for 6/15 - proposed times in the calendar invite I just sent

Notes on potential regression risk:
- If you switch to a larger model + dense-only retriever, you may see improved recall at cost of latency and higher token cost. We'll monitor quality regressions against the 50 canonical queries and flag any drop >5% precision@3 as a regression.

Attachments: acme_rag_eval_plan.pdf, acme_prompt_sets_v1.zip, benchmark_results_summary.csv

Thanks - open to questions and happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

2) On model licensing/cost: LM choices look fine - can you include estimated cost per 1k requests for each model combo in the SOW?

Also looping in Alex Gomez (search infra) to validate export format - Alex, can you confirm if we can export the docs to a single S3 prefix in JSONL?

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RAG pilot kickoff - recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Alex -

Quick answers: 
- Reranker latency: with MonoBERT-v1 cross-encoder we typically see an additive latency of ~60-130ms for rerank on top6 in our us-west region depending on batch packing; combined with a well-tuned retriever and token-limited generator that should keep p95 in the 500-650ms band. Dev will provide a short perf note.
- Cost estimates: SOW will contain per-1k request cost for each model+retriever combo and an assumed token distribution - we will call out quantized options separately (Llama-3 quantized will be substantially cheaper).

Action items noted on our side. Alex - thanks for taking point on the export; if you can confirm S3 prefix and sample file by EOD Fri, that would help us start ingestion Monday.

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sam Irwin <sam@acme.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.io>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Perf note: reranker impact & tuning knobs

Folks -

Following up on the reranker latency question. High-level:
- MonoBERT-v1 (cross-encoder) runtime for top6 after dense retrieval: median ~45ms, p95 ~110-130ms per request in a well-packed batch on our dedicated infra.
- Key knobs to control tail latency:
  * Batch packing (we can do dynamic batching up to 64 reqs - reduces p95 substantially)
  * Use reranker only on queries flagged as low-confidence by the generator (adaptive reranking)
  * Reduce rerank top_k to 4 for tighter latency SLOs (will impact precision@3 marginally)

If ACME wants tighter p95 budget (<=500ms), recommend: top_k retrieve=10, rerank top_k=4, adaptive reranking enabled. Happy to provide a quick perf deck.

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
